column2: The Lord speaks to Moses, introducing the festival calendar rather than a new narrative event.
The feasts are proclaimed as holy convocations and identified as Mine. The repeated feast designation is retained.
Six workdays contrast with seventh-day rest and no work. Singular commands precede the plural dwelling reference, preserved through ordinary you.
The appointed times qualify proclamation of the convocations. Proper times is temporal, not a new evaluation of their merits.
Fourteenth day of the first month and between the evenings remain exact. No modern clock time is imposed.
The fifteenth begins seven days of unleavened bread. The festival and eating duration remain distinct statements.
The first day is holy; laborious work renders the qualified work term, distinguished from the unqualified prohibition in verse 3.
Seven days of offerings culminate in seventh-day convocation and the qualified work prohibition. Neither repeated requirement is omitted.
A separate speech introduces the first-harvest instruction.
Land entry and harvest lead to bringing a sheaf as first portion to the priest. The sheaf is not replaced with a measured grain quantity.
The Greek says the morrow after the first, not after the Sabbath here. Day is a necessary contextual supply, kept distinct from verse 15.
The sheaf day requires an unblemished year-old animal designated probaton. Sheep remains provisional without adding male where not expressed.
Two tenths of flour and a quarter hin of wine remain distinct accompanying gifts. Ancient measures are not converted without evidence.
Bread and roasted fresh grain are withheld until presentation. The Greek's compact grain wording is not expanded into a third independent category.
column3: Does the adjective/participle grouping imply separate roasted and fresh-grain categories or the inherited combined phrase?

column2: Counting begins after the Sabbath and the sheaf presentation, extending seven complete weeks. Both starting descriptions remain.
Fifty days reaches the day after the final week and a new sacrifice. The inclusive counting is not modernized by assumption.
Two loaves from two tenths are explicitly leavened. They are presented as firstfruits; no altar burning is stated here.
Seven lambs, one calf and two rams accompany the loaves with their sacrifices and libations. Unblemished is not inserted into a different grammatical location.
The source shifts to they for the goat and two lambs. The lambs' deliverance role differs from the preceding whole offerings.
The priest presents the items with loaves and lambs; they become his portion. The repeated presentation wording remains without a specified waving motion.
Proclamation, holiness, no laborious work and enduring observance across dwellings all remain in the instruction.
Harvest remainder and fallen produce are left for poor and resident foreigner. The singular/plural address shifts do not justify adding all to you.
A new speech introduces the seventh-month first-day observance.
Rest and a memorial of trumpets identify the first day. The plural instruments are not reduced to an unspecified sound.
No laborious work accompanies a whole offering. The qualified prohibition remains consistent with the other festival days.
A separate divine speech introduces the tenth-day atonement observance.
Tenth day, holy convocation, self-humbling and whole offering remain. A fasting instruction is not inserted as an explicit Greek verb.
The work prohibition is unqualified here, grounded in atonement before the Lord. The broader scope differs from laborious work elsewhere.
Failure to be humbled brings destruction from the people. The passive formulation does not identify an execution method.
The Greek says that person shall perish; the source does not explicitly say I will destroy in this clause.
No work is repeated as a lasting rule in all dwellings. The explicit all is retained.
The ninth day's evening begins the evening-to-evening Sabbath observance. The temporal detail is not shifted to the tenth morning.
A new divine speech introduces the Feast of Tents.
The feast begins on the fifteenth of the seventh month and lasts seven days. Its name retains the tent image.
First-day convocation and prohibition of laborious work are explicit. No restriction on all work is substituted.
Seven days of offerings precede eighth-day convocation and closing observance. Closing renders exodion provisionally without importing an assembly term from another base.
The summary lists whole offerings, their sacrifices and libations, apportioned day by day. Daily requirement is an idiomatic supply for the distributive expression.
Sabbaths, gifts, all vows and freewill offerings are additional categories. The repeated besides is source-supported.
The harvest completion and fifteenth-day feast include rest on first and eighth days. Seven-day celebration and eighth-day rest are both retained.
Fruit, palm fronds, dense branches, willows and chaste-tree branches all appear in this Greek list. The last botanical item is not omitted.
column3: Confirm horaios as beautiful versus seasonable/ripe and the exact botanical labels without harmonizing the list.

column2: Of the year continues the preceding seven days. The short source verse is not expanded into a new independent celebration clause.
Seven-day tent residence applies to every native in Israel. The explicit native designation is retained.
Future generations are to see that God settled Israel in tents during the exodus. See preserves the selected verb without narrowing it to literal eyewitness presence.
Moses communicates the Lord's feasts to Israel, closing the calendar speeches.
The Lord addresses Moses before the lamp and bread instructions.
Pure beaten olive oil supplies a continually burning lamp. Continually is explicit in the duration phrase, not an ornamental addition.
Aaron and his sons burn it from evening to morning outside the veil. Both the named sons and recurrent observance are present.
Plural lamps on the pure lampstand burn until morning in this Greek. The time clause is not replaced by a general continual formula.
Twelve loaves each contain two tenths. The unstated measure name is not invented within the verse.
Two arrangements of six stand on the pure table. Arrangements leaves rows versus stacks open.
Frankincense and salt are both named. They serve as the bread's memorial; salt is not omitted to match another text.
column3: Confirm the relation of the plural memorial objects to the loaves in the final clause.

column2: Weekly presentation is before the Lord and before Israel as an enduring covenant. The singular presenter remains implicit.
Aaron and sons eat in a holy place, with most-holy status and perpetual entitlement. Singular and plural references are retained.
The man's Israelite mother and Egyptian father are explicit; the fight is with an Israelite man in camp.
Pronouncing the Name and cursing are two expressions. Shelomith and Dibri retain inherited name forms provisionally rather than being normalized from transliteration alone.
Custody serves judgment through the Lord's command. The source does not specify how long confinement lasted.
The divine answer is addressed to Moses before the public instructions.
All hearers lay hands before the whole congregation stones the offender. These groups and actions remain distinct.
Cursing God brings sin-bearing. The following naming clause must not be silently collapsed into the same verb.
The selected Greek repeatedly says naming the Lord's name. The draft retains it rather than substituting blaspheming, with the narrative context still available.
column3: Does the context restrict naming to abusive invocation? Record that interpretation separately from the explicit wording.

column2: A strike resulting in the person's death triggers the death sanction. The victim's death is an explicit condition.
Animal death entails repayment, life for life. Repayment distinguishes this clause from the preceding human-death sanction.
Injury to a neighbour receives reciprocal treatment. As done and as repaid preserve the comparison.
Fracture, eye and tooth form the specific examples, followed by the general injury rule. No additional penalty is inserted.
The Greek repeats the human-death case here without a repeated animal-repayment clause. That source-specific omission is preserved.
One judgment applies to resident foreigner and local inhabitant. The legal term is contextual judgment rather than a doctrinal justification claim.
Moses speaks, the people take the offender out and stone him, and obedience is stated. All three narrative stages remain.
